# Text


<!-- WARNING: THIS FILE WAS AUTOGENERATED! DO NOT EDIT! -->

Names and headers are drawn as live text, so their size comes from the
font itself.
[`text_width`](https://adamcc.github.io/itemiset/core/text.html#text_width)
measures a string from the font’s outlines, which is what decides how
wide a cell or a header must be.

Header labels sometimes need more than one line.
[`wrap_label`](https://adamcc.github.io/itemiset/core/text.html#wrap_label)
breaks a label only at places a reader would accept: between words
first, then at a **soft hyphen** (U+00AD) the label’s author put in,
then after a dash that is already there. Writing `"Argo\u00adnautes"` in
a label says *break here if you must*; the soft hyphen is invisible
otherwise.

Dictionary hyphenation is optional (`hyphenate=True`, which needs the
`pyphen` package: `pip install itemiset[hyphen]`). It is off by default
so that the same labels break the same way on every computer, whether or
not `pyphen` is installed.

### text_width

``` python
def text_width(
    s:str, size:float, font:str='DejaVu Sans', weight:int=400, style:str='normal'
)->float:
```

*Advance width of `s` in points, measured from the outlines of `font` at
`size` points.*

Widths grow with the text and with the size, and an empty string takes
no room:

``` python
test_eq(text_width("", 7), 0.0)
w = text_width("CNOT10", 7)
assert 0 < w < text_width("CNOT10 CNOT10", 7)
test_close(text_width("CNOT10", 14), 2 * w, eps=0.05 * w)
assert text_width("CNOT10", 7, weight=700) > w   # bold is wider
```

## Breaking labels over lines

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/adamcc/itemiset/blob/main/itemiset/core/text.py#L53"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### wrap_label

``` python
def wrap_label(
    label:str, fits, hyphenate:bool=False
)->list | None:
```

*Break `label` into lines that each satisfy `fits(line)`, or return None
if a piece cannot fit.*

Whole words move to the next line before any word is broken. A word too
long for a line is broken at its soft hyphens if it has any; otherwise,
with `hyphenate=True`, at dictionary points (en_US, via pyphen);
otherwise anywhere leaving three or more letters on each side. A hyphen
is added at the break unless the line already ends with a dash.

The examples measure lines in characters, so the rules are easy to see:
`upto(n)` accepts lines of at most `n` characters.

``` python
upto = lambda n: (lambda t: len(t) <= n)
test_eq(wrap_label("Central metabolism", upto(20)), ["Central metabolism"])
test_eq(wrap_label("Central metabolism", upto(10)), ["Central", "metabolism"])   # whole words first
test_eq(wrap_label("Argo\u00adnautes", upto(6)), ["Argo-", "nautes"])         # the author's break point
test_eq(wrap_label("CCR4–NOT", upto(6)), ["CCR4–", "NOT"])                    # no hyphen after a dash
test_eq(wrap_label("Photosynthesis", upto(9)), ["Photosyn-", "thesis"])        # 3+ letters each side
test_eq(wrap_label("Photosynthesis", upto(3)), None)                           # cannot fit
```

The soft hyphen never shows unless a line breaks there:

``` python
test_eq(wrap_label("De\u00adcapping complex", upto(20)), ["Decapping complex"])
test_eq(wrap_label("De\u00adcapping complex", upto(8)), ["De-", "capping", "complex"])
```
